set.approach: Drive the Snaring road past the campsites to where it turns to dirt; after the big U-turn above Jasper Lake the crag is on the left as the road descends, and parking is on the right by the open field. Walk up the powerline line to the second pole, then a little farther on angle right up scrambly ground to top out the lower, chossy cliff band. The routes are on the obvious low-angle slabs above it, on sharp rock.
set.descent_text: The anchors sit well back from the top of the climbs, so lowering drags the rope across the rock and wears it.

review.notes: Crag-level approach from area page; no route-specific location available.

set.approach: Park at the end of the guardrail just past the 17 Mile sign outside Haines. Drop into the ditch, follow the creek past the culvert, and pick up the flagged trail that climbs into the woods to a boulder field. For the Bear Spray Wall, leave the main trail and head up and to the right until you meet a second flagged trail, which passes several small loose cliffs before reaching the wall.

set.approach: Drive up Red Rock Canyon to about halfway, past the large red debris pile nearest the road, and park at one of the pullouts beyond it. Find the prominent ridge running up to the canyon rim and climb it with only a short bit of bushwhacking to the west rim, then cross the tundra plateau to the east rim. The crags sit at the top of the plateau just to the south, nearer Canwell Peak.

set.approach: Thumb Cove is on the east side of Resurrection Bay, south of Seward, and is reached by paddle, motorboat or water taxi from town. Check tides, weather and the marine forecast before going. Some undeveloped parts of the cove have difficult foot access.

set.approach: The crag is reached from Highway 28 by one of three parking lots, and each lot gives access to all of the climbing, so park at the one nearest the wall you want. A maintained trail system with stairs and bridges links the lots to the crags.
set.descent_text: Routes finish at bolted anchors with bolted rappel stations, so parties descend by rappelling from the stations. The top of each crag can also be reached by an easy trail or scramble, which makes top-roping practical.

set.approach: From the pack station where the Pine Creek road ends, take the Pine Creek Pass Trail for about 2.8 miles. The wall is on the left a short distance from the trail, with no off-trail travel needed. The point where you step off the trail puts you at the buttress's left side. The trail is sunny while the climbing is shaded, so an early start helps.
